transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, most days I wake up and it just feels like there's this heavy, gray weight sitting on me. It's hard to explain, but it's just this constant low, hollow feeling. Even when I'm out working with the landscaping crew, or, you know, at home around my kids, I just can't shake it. It feels like I'm just going through the motions of everything.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been a long time. I'd say it's been going on for about three years and three months now. It started right around the time the groundskeeping contract changed at work. They shifted our schedule, and those longer days just kind of took over my life. I've felt this way ever since.
Have you ever had times in your life where you felt the complete opposite—unusually energized, wired, or on top of the world, needing very little sleep?

No, I... I can't say I have. I don't think I've ever felt wired or on top of the world like that. Honestly, with the physical work I do, I'm usually pretty beat by the end of the day, so I definitely need my sleep. It's really just been this same heavy, low feeling the whole time.
Over these past three years, have you had any breaks where your mood returned to normal for two months or more?

No, I haven't. I mean... maybe I'll have a decent afternoon here or there, but a whole two months? No. It never really lifts for that long. It's pretty much just been this same heavy feeling the entire time.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight during this time?
No, not really. I mean, my weight has stayed pretty much the same, as far as I can tell. I guess I still eat about what I usually do. So... no, no real changes there.
How has your sleep been over these past few years—have you had trouble falling or staying asleep, or finding yourself sleeping too much?

No, my sleep has been alright. Like I said earlier, with the landscaping work, I'm pretty worn out by the end of the day. So... I usually just fall right asleep. I don't really have trouble staying asleep, and I'm not sleeping more than usual, either. It's pretty much just my regular amount.
How have you been feeling about yourself during this time—have you noticed your self-esteem or confidence slipping?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I know I'm good at my job, and I know how to do the work. I don't really feel bad about myself, I just... I just feel down all the time. But my confidence is fine, I guess. I haven't noticed any changes with that.
Looking ahead, have you been feeling hopeless about your future or feeling like things won't get better?

Yeah, I do. I just... I keep telling myself that this is just how my life is now. It feels like no matter how hard I work, or how much I try to get back to doing things I used to care about—like working in my own garden or going to those music nights—nothing is really going to turn around. It just feels like this is it, and it's not going to get any better.
Have you had any trouble concentrating or making everyday decisions?

No, I haven't really noticed any problems with that. I mean, my job is pretty routine, so I don't have to make a lot of big decisions or think too hard about what I'm doing. I just kind of go through the motions. But no, I wouldn't say I have trouble concentrating.
How has your energy level been over this time—have you felt constantly low on energy or unusually fatigued?

Yeah, the fatigue is pretty constant. By midmorning, my body feels like I've already put in a full day of work. And it doesn't really matter how much rest I get. Even after sleeping in on a Sunday, I still just drag through simple things... you know, like loading up my tools for the week, checking over the job plans, or even just making dinner. It's just a constant low energy.
